To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The use of a thin film of an optically active material as solid support for single molecule fluorescence detection allows to use the nonlinear optical properties of the film for the efficient fluorescence excitation of single molecules.

(1) the frequency doubling of a laser beam in a thin layer of optically nonlinear material is feasible; (2) the fluorescence excitation of a molecule by the frequency doubled light in a thin layer is feasible and efficient; and (3) the fluorescence excite of a molecule by frequency doubling in a thin layer can be much more efficient than a two-photon fluorescence excite.

(1) the fluorescence excitation of single molecules by a second harmonic generated in a nonlinear material is feasible and (2) the fluorescence intensity can be increased by a factor of 2.5-3.5, compared to a two-photon fluorescence excitaton, when the molecules are immobilised on the nonlinear material.
